model.name: Organizational Unit
model.purpose: Provide the format-neutral context an agent needs to understand, create, inspect and operate the internal structure of an organization: which units exist, how they nest and report, what each is mandated to do, what establishment and staffing they carry, and how that structure is changed, dated, evidenced and disclosed over time.
model.scope_statement: This model covers an organizational unit as a subdivision that, in the words of the W3C Organization Ontology, 'only has full recognition within the context of that Organization'. It governs unit identity, classification, containment and reporting relationships, delegated mandate and decision rights, authorized establishment and measured staffing, structural change acts and their temporal validity, plus the provenance, retention, disclosure and interoperability rules that make the structure record operable. It deliberately stops at the boundaries of legal organizational identity, of the post/position as an object in its own right, of employment relationships, of physical sites, and of statistical or financial reporting units that are derived from - but not identical to - internal structure.
in_scope: Unit identity, naming, aliases and parent-scoped or ISO/IEC 6523 organization-part identification
Unit kind classification against governed code lists and unit existence status
Containment hierarchies, including multiple concurrent hierarchies (managerial, legal, cost, functional)
Reporting and coordination lines, including non-containment and dotted-line relationships
Delegated mandate, decision rights, authority limits and segregation-of-duties constraints attached to a unit
Authorized establishment (post complement) seated in a unit and its occupancy state at unit granularity
Dated headcount and full-time-equivalent measurement of a unit, with basis and aggregation thresholds
Reorganization acts (create, rename, reparent, merge, split, transfer, disband) and unit lineage
Effective dating, bitemporality and as-of reconstruction of the structure graph
Record authority, approval evidence, retention/disposition and disclosure control for structure data
Crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 projections
out_of_scope: Legal personality, incorporation, registration, LEI and regulatory identity of the whole organization (WM-ORG-001)
The post/position as an object with its own title, grade, job description and occupational classification (WM-ORG-004)
Employment contracts, appointments, persons and their occupancy of posts
Constitutive charter powers of the organization as a legal entity (charter model)
Physical premises, addresses, geometry and site operations (site/location model)
Statistical units such as enterprise, local unit and kind-of-activity unit used for economic observation
Financial segment reporting, general ledger and cost accounting mechanics
Stewardship policy machinery and access-grant issuance (S1/S2 service models)
Business capability, process and value-stream modelling
Identity-provider group membership and directory synchronisation state as a system of record

boundary_notes.distinction: W3C ORG separates org:FormalOrganization (recognized in a legal jurisdiction, with rights and responsibilities) from org:OrganizationalUnit, which has full recognition only inside its parent. Legal identity, registration and LEI stay in WM-ORG-001. A branch that is separately registered is dual-classified: it is a unit here and a legal entity there, and GLEIF only issues an LEI to the legally registered entity, not to an internal division.

org:Post represents a position that exists independently of who fills it. This model records only the unit-side facts: how many posts are established in the unit, which posts are seated there, and the aggregate occupancy state. Post title, grade, competency profile and occupational classification belong to WM-ORG-004, which this model CONTAINS by reference rather than by copy.

FHIR states that Location records where a service occurs while Organization records who performed it; Eurostat's 'local unit' is 'an enterprise or part thereof ... situated in a geographically identified place'. A unit may be associated with one or more sites, but premises, addresses and geometry are not unit attributes and are not modelled here.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 defines enterprise, kind-of-activity unit and local unit as observation units for economic statistics. These are derived by statistical rules from operational reality, not asserted by the organization, and their boundaries routinely differ from internal units. Treated as an ALIGN target, never as a source of internal unit identity.

IFRS 8 identifies operating segments through a management approach based on how the chief operating decision maker reviews internal reports, and permits aggregation of segments with similar economic characteristics. A reportable segment is therefore a derived view over internal units, not a unit; this model supplies the inputs and the change signal, not the segment determination.

RFC 4519 defines 'ou' as a multi-valued name attribute and RFC 7643 defines SCIM 'department', 'division' and 'organization' as free-text names. These carry no identifier, no validity period and no hierarchy semantics, so directory content is a lossy projection of this model and never its system of record.

ROR states it 'is not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change'. No general governed global identifier exists for internal units, so unit identity is parent-scoped by default.

sources.title: The Organization Ontology
sources.relevance: Normative definitions of org:OrganizationalUnit, org:hasUnit/org:unitOf, org:subOrganizationOf, org:Post, org:reportsTo, org:Membership, org:Role, org:Site, org:purpose, org:classification, org:identifier and org:ChangeEvent with org:originalOrganization/org:resultingOrganization. Primary structural anchor for this model.

sources.title: FHIR R5 Resource Organization
sources.version_or_date: FHIR v5.0.0 (R5), 26 March 2023, Maturity Level 5 / Trial Use
sources.relevance: Counter-model in which departments are Organization instances chained by partOf rather than a distinct unit class; supplies identifier/active/type/name/alias/qualification elements, the 'at least one name or identifier' constraint, the Organization-vs-Location boundary, and OrganizationAffiliation for non-hierarchical relationships.

sources.title: Core Public Organisation Vocabulary (CPOV)
sources.version_or_date: v2.1.2, SEMIC Recommendation, released 2026-05-12; namespace http://data.europa.eu/m8g/
sources.relevance: Public-sector profile reusing org:Organization and org:OrganizationalUnit ('a subdivision of Organization which is part of this Organization'), with hasUnit, hasSubOrganization, purpose (COFOG-coded), classification and spatial. Evidence that unit purpose/classification are code-valued and scheme-bound in the public sector.

sources.title: RFC 4519: Lightweight Directory Access Protocol (LDAP): Schema for User Applications
sources.relevance: Defines the 'organizationalUnit' object class as 'the basis of an entry that represents a piece of an organization' and 'ou' as a multi-valued name attribute. Establishes the directory projection and its loss of identifier, validity and typed-edge semantics.

sources.title: RFC 7643: System for Cross-domain Identity Management: Core Schema
sources.relevance: Enterprise User extension defines 'department', 'division', 'organization' and 'costCenter' purely as names, and 'manager' as the only typed reference. Primary evidence that HR/IdP interchange formats are name-valued and cannot round-trip unit identity or hierarchy.

sources.title: RFC 3339: Date and Time on the Internet: Timestamps
sources.relevance: Normative timestamp format: date-time requires a time-offset of 'Z' or a numeric offset; '-00:00' signals a known UTC instant with unknown local offset. Governs decision date, effective date and observation/ingestion time recording throughout this model.

sources.title: Peppol BIS Billing 3.0 - ISO 6523 ICD code list
sources.relevance: Operational registry of ISO/IEC 6523 International Code Designators (e.g. 0060 D-U-N-S, 0088 GLN, 0192 Norwegian organisasjonsnummer, 0208 Belgian enterprise number) used as schemeID for party identification, including delivery-location and payee parties. Anchors the ICD + organization identifier + organization part identifier addressing pattern for units.

sources.title: schema.org Organization
sources.relevance: Defines department ('a relationship between an organization and a department of that organization'), parentOrganization (superseding branchOf), subOrganization, numberOfEmployees, and identifier properties iso6523Code (XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ), leiCode, duns and naics. Shows publication-facing conflation of department and subsidiary.

sources.title: IFRS 8 Operating Segments
sources.organization: IFRS Foundation / International Accounting Standards Board
sources.relevance: Management approach: segments follow how management internally organizes the entity and how the chief operating decision maker reviews internal reports; aggregation criteria and quantitative thresholds apply, and when internal structure changes prior-period segment information must be restated or the change disclosed. Establishes downstream obligations triggered by reorganization.

sources.title: Glossary: Local unit (Statistics Explained)
sources.version_or_date: Eurostat glossary entry citing Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/1993 of 15 March 1993
sources.relevance: Definition of a local unit as 'an enterprise or part thereof (e.g. a workshop, factory, warehouse, office, mine or depot) situated in a geographically identified place', with kind-of-activity unit as the activity-based counterpart. Used to keep statistical observation units outside this model's boundary.

sources.title: ROR Data Structure (schema 2.1)
sources.version_or_date: Schema 2.1, launched December 2024; documentation updated 20 May 2026
sources.relevance: Working registry model for organizational relationships: parent, child, related, predecessor and successor, with reciprocal edges on active records and tombstoned edges on inactive/withdrawn records; status values active/inactive/withdrawn; admin created and last_modified with schema version. Directly informs lineage and versioning design.

sources.title: ROR FAQs
sources.relevance: Explicit scope exclusion: ROR 'is not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change' while higher-level information is 'more stable and is therefore better suited for persistence'. Key falsifying evidence against assuming global unit identifiers.

sources.title: The Legal Entity Identifier (LEI)
sources.version_or_date: Accessed 24 August 2026; LEI per ISO 17442; GLEIF established 2014
sources.relevance: LEI is a 20-character code where 'every LEI is unique and can represent only one entity'; Level 1 'who is who' and Level 2 'who owns whom' data cover legal entities and ownership, not internal divisions. Bounds unit identity away from legal-entity identity.

sources.title: ISO 37000 Governance of organizations - Guidance (ISO/TC 309 overview)
sources.relevance: Accountability is established by assigning responsibility and delegating authority; those who delegate remain accountable for the delegate's use of that authority; delegation should be formalized with assurance processes; and no one should be accountable for matters over which they have no authority. Normative backbone for the mandate and authority-limit findings.

sources.title: ESRS S1 Own Workforce (Annex I, Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772)
sources.version_or_date: Commission Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/2772 of 31 July 2023, Annex I
sources.relevance: Disclosure Requirement S1-6 obliges reporting of total employees by head count and/or full-time equivalent with breakdowns by gender and by country (countries with 50 or more employees among the ten largest), plus methodology disclosure. External constraint on how headcount snapshots must be defined, dated and aggregated.

sources.title: General Records Schedules (GRS)
sources.organization: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)
sources.version_or_date: Page last reviewed 12 June 2026; GRS status updates June 2026
sources.relevance: Disposition authority for common records: use of the GRS is mandatory and 'agencies must use the GRS unless they can justify the use of an agency-specific schedule'; GRS covers administrative and support functions rather than mission records. Model for binding a governed disposition authority to structure records.

bundles.name: Unit Identity and Classification
bundles.description: What a unit is, how it is unambiguously referenced, what it is called, what kind of thing it is, and whether it currently exists.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG makes the unit a class whose recognition is parent-scoped, while ROR and GLEIF decline to issue global identifiers for subdivisions. Identity and classification therefore need explicit, locally governed treatment before any structural claim can be made.

layers.name: Unit Identification
layers.description: Identifier assignment, external addressability and naming of a unit.

findings.name: Unit Identifier Scheme and Assignment
findings.description: A unit's authoritative identifier is normally minted by the parent organization's master system, because no general governed global registry issues identifiers for internal subdivisions. ISO/IEC 6523 provides the only widely deployed external addressing slot, combining an International Code Designator, the parent organization identifier and an optional organization part identifier; schema.org exposes this as iso6523Code in XXXX:YYYYYY:ZZZ form. Identifier stability across rename, reparenting and merge must be decided explicitly.

questions.text: Which system is the authoritative assigner of this unit's identifier, and is that system the parent organization's master record rather than a downstream HR or directory system?
Can this unit be addressed externally as an ISO/IEC 6523 organization part under the parent organization's ICD and organization identifier, and if so which OPI value and source indicator apply?
Does the identifier survive renaming, reparenting and merger of the unit, and is it guaranteed never to be reassigned to a different unit?
answer_data: events that force a new identifier

questions.text: If no master-system identifier exists, which UUID or ULID does the adopting Dimension mint, and where is that minting act recorded?

data_elements.name: unitIdentifier
data_elements.description: The authoritative identifier for the unit within its assigning scheme.

data_elements.name: unitIdentifierScheme
data_elements.description: Coded reference to the scheme and assigning authority for the identifier.

data_elements.name: organizationPartIdentifier
data_elements.description: ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identifier for external addressing of the unit, with its source indicator.

data_elements.name: alternateIdentifiers
data_elements.description: Non-authoritative identifiers held in downstream systems (ERP cost centre code, LDAP DN, IdP group id).

artifacts.name: Unit Identifier Register
artifacts.description: The authoritative register of unit identifiers, their scheme, assignment act and retirement state, held by the parent organization.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Registered under the parent organization's master-system register identifier; each entry keyed by unitIdentifier, which is never reused.

findings.name: Unit Naming and Designation
findings.description: Units carry an official name, display and short names, abbreviations, language variants and superseded historical names. FHIR provides name plus alias for 'alternate or historical names' and requires at least one name or identifier; LDAP 'ou' is explicitly multi-valued. Names are unstable and non-unique and must never be used as identity.

questions.text: Which name is the official designation of the unit, in which language, and which instrument fixed it?
Which former names remain in use downstream and over which validity periods were they current?
Is the unit name required to be unique within its parent, within the whole organization, or not at all?

data_elements.name: officialName
data_elements.description: The official designation of the unit, with language tag.

data_elements.name: alias
data_elements.description: Alternate, short, acronym or historical names with type and validity period.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Names and aliases are attribute-level values carried inline on the unit record and rendered into other artifacts (register, org chart, directory export). No separate governed artifact is produced by naming alone.

layers.name: Unit Classification and Existence
layers.description: The kind of unit and whether it currently exists as an operating subdivision.

findings.name: Unit Kind and Classification Scheme
findings.description: Units are typed against a governed code list (department, division, directorate, branch, committee, board, team, programme office, shared-service centre, cost centre). W3C ORG provides org:classification against a scheme; CPOV constrains purpose to COFOG codes for public organisations and adds a classification property; FHIR uses a CodeableConcept type. The scheme must be named, versioned and resolvable, and the same unit may carry codes from several schemes simultaneously.

questions.text: Against which named and versioned classification scheme is the unit's kind asserted, and is that scheme resolvable to a published code list?
Does the unit carry codes from more than one scheme (internal kind, public-sector function, industry activity), and which one governs behaviour?
Is this subdivision also a formal organization recognized in a legal jurisdiction, requiring dual classification and a link to WM-ORG-001?
What evidence is required before a unit's kind may be reclassified, and does reclassification require a reorganization act?

data_elements.name: unitKind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of unit against a governed scheme.

data_elements.name: classificationScheme
data_elements.description: Identifier and version of the scheme from which each code is drawn.

data_elements.name: isAlsoFormalOrganization
data_elements.description: Whether this subdivision is separately recognized as a legal entity.

artifacts.name: Unit Kind Code List
artifacts.description: The governed, versioned code list of unit kinds used by the adopting Dimension, with definitions, deprecations and mappings to org:classification and CPOV codes.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by a governed scheme IRI plus semantic version; codes are never reused after deprecation.

findings.name: Unit Existence Status
findings.description: Whether the unit is proposed, active, dormant, suspended, disbanded or created in error. FHIR carries a boolean 'active'; ROR distinguishes active, inactive and withdrawn, where withdrawn means the record was created in error and is not a real-world cessation. That three-way distinction - operating, ceased, erroneous - is required so that error correction is not confused with reorganization.

questions.text: Which status values are permitted for a unit, and is 'created in error' modelled separately from 'ceased to operate'?
Which status transitions are legal, and which of them require a reorganization act rather than a simple correction?
How is a unit that exists on paper but has no establishment and no activity represented, and how long may it stay in that state?
After a unit is disbanded, is its record tombstoned with its relationships retained for historical reconstruction, or removed?

data_elements.name: unitStatus
data_elements.description: Current lifecycle status of the unit from the governed status vocabulary.

data_elements.name: statusEffectiveFrom
data_elements.description: The instant from which the current status applies.

data_elements.name: withdrawalReason
data_elements.description: Reason a record was withdrawn as erroneous, distinct from real-world disbandment.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Status is a single governed attribute on the unit record; its history is materialised by the versioning artifacts in the temporal-validity layer rather than by a separate artifact here.

bundles.name: Structural Composition
bundles.description: How units nest into hierarchies and how they report to and coordinate with one another.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG separates containment (org:hasUnit, org:subOrganizationOf) from reporting (org:reportsTo), FHIR separates partOf hierarchy from OrganizationAffiliation, and IFRS 8's management approach shows that more than one concurrent view of structure is normal. Composition therefore needs two distinct layers rather than one tree.

layers.name: Containment Hierarchy
layers.description: Parent-child membership of units within the organization, including concurrent hierarchies.

findings.name: Parent-Child Containment
findings.description: Every unit resolves to exactly one parent organization and, except at the top, to one parent unit within a given hierarchy. W3C ORG expresses this with org:unitOf/org:hasUnit and org:subOrganizationOf; FHIR uses partOf; schema.org uses parentOrganization, which supersedes branchOf and is not distinguished from subsidiary ownership. ROR maintains reciprocal parent and child edges on active records. Cycles, orphans and multi-parent assertions within one hierarchy are integrity failures.

questions.text: Which organization (WM-ORG-001 instance) does this unit ultimately belong to, and is that link mandatory and immutable for the unit's lifetime?
Which unit is the immediate parent within the named hierarchy, and what is the depth and root of that path?
How are cycles, orphaned units and multiple parents within a single hierarchy detected and prevented at write time?

Is the parent link a containment of a non-legal subdivision or an ownership relation to a separate legal entity, and how is that difference preserved when exporting to vocabularies that conflate them?

data_elements.name: parentOrganizationRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the WM-ORG-001 organization instance that owns the structure.

data_elements.name: parentUnitRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the immediate parent unit within a named hierarchy.

data_elements.name: hierarchyPath
data_elements.description: Ordered path of unit identifiers from the hierarchy root to this unit, derived not asserted.

artifacts.name: Organization Chart Projection
artifacts.description: A rendered or serialised view of the containment hierarchy with unit names and kinds, deliberately omitting mandate detail and staffing figures.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by hierarchy name plus as-of instant (RFC 3339) plus source structure version; regenerated projections are new serial instances, never edits.

findings.name: Concurrent Hierarchies and Matrix Structure
findings.description: One organization commonly maintains several simultaneous hierarchies over the same units: managerial line, legal-entity roll-up, cost/budget roll-up, functional or professional line, and the internal reporting structure that IFRS 8 makes decisive for segment identification. Each hierarchy is a separately named, separately governed edge set; collapsing them into one tree destroys the information that downstream reporting depends on.

questions.text: Which named hierarchies exist over the unit set, who owns each, and which one is the default for display?
Where does a unit's position differ between hierarchies, and is that divergence intentional or an integrity defect?
Which hierarchy corresponds to the internal reports reviewed by the chief operating decision maker for the purposes of segment identification?
When two hierarchies imply conflicting authority over the same unit, which precedence rule resolves the conflict?

data_elements.name: hierarchyIdentifier
data_elements.description: Identifier and purpose of a named hierarchy over the unit set.

data_elements.name: hierarchyEdge
data_elements.description: A parent-child edge qualified by hierarchy identifier and validity period.

data_elements.name: isCodmReportingHierarchy
data_elements.description: Marks the hierarchy that reflects internal management reporting for segment purposes.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Concurrent hierarchies are edge sets over the units already registered elsewhere; each materialises through the org chart projection artifact parameterised by hierarchy identifier, so no additional artifact class is warranted.

layers.name: Reporting and Coordination
layers.description: Directed reporting relations and non-containment relationships between units.

findings.name: Reporting Lines and Their Standards Basis
findings.description: Reporting lines are distinct from containment: a unit may sit under one parent but report functionally elsewhere (dotted line). W3C ORG's org:reportsTo is defined between Agents or Posts, not between organizational units, so unit-to-unit reporting is an extension of the standard and must be declared as such rather than claimed as conformant. SCIM offers only a single 'manager' reference at person level, which cannot carry line type or validity.

questions.text: What type is each reporting line - administrative, functional, professional, operational or advisory - and is it solid or dotted?
Does the reporting line hold between units, between posts, or between the units' heads, and which representation is authoritative?
answer_data: derivation rule for the other representations

questions.text: Where unit-to-unit reporting is asserted, is the departure from org:reportsTo recorded as an explicit extension with a mapping rule?
Over which period is each reporting line valid, and can two lines of the same type to different targets overlap in time?

data_elements.name: reportingLine
data_elements.description: Directed reporting relation with type, subject kind, target and validity period.

data_elements.name: reportingLineType
data_elements.description: Coded type of the reporting relation.

data_elements.name: standardExtensionNote
data_elements.description: Declaration that unit-level reporting extends beyond the domain/range of org:reportsTo.

artifacts.name: Reporting Line Matrix
artifacts.description: Edge list of all reporting relations with type, direction, validity and standards-mapping note, usable for matrix-management analysis and for detecting conflicting lines.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by organization identifier plus as-of instant (RFC 3339); each generation is a new serial instance referencing the structure version it was derived from.

findings.name: Cross-Unit and External Affiliations
findings.description: Units participate in relations that are neither containment nor reporting: shared services, joint committees, secondments of capacity, service-level relations to other units, and affiliations to bodies in other legal entities. FHIR introduces OrganizationAffiliation precisely for 'complex non-hierarchical relationships between separate legal entities without implying ownership'; ROR uses a 'related' type for 'less defined connections, such as resource sharing or participation without direct control'.

questions.text: What kind of non-hierarchical relation is this - shared service, joint body, service agreement, secondment or partnership - and does it imply any control?
Does the counterparty sit inside the same parent organization or in a different legal entity, and does that change which model owns the relation?
Which instrument establishes the affiliation, over what period, and what obligations does it place on the unit?

data_elements.name: unitAffiliation
data_elements.description: Non-hierarchical relation between a unit and another unit or external body, with type and validity.

data_elements.name: affiliationInstrumentRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the agreement or decision that establishes the affiliation.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Affiliations are reference data resolved against counterparty records held by WM-ORG-001 or by contract models; the establishing instrument is an artifact of those models, not of this one.

bundles.name: Mandate and Authority
bundles.description: What a unit is empowered to do, within which limits, and who is accountable for it.
bundles.rationale: ISO 37000 makes accountability a product of assigned responsibility and delegated authority, holds that delegators remain accountable, and requires delegation to be formalized. W3C ORG's org:purpose and CPOV's code-valued purpose give the vocabulary; the limits, controls and accountability holder are the operating surface.

layers.name: Remit and Decision Rights
layers.description: The scope of a unit's mandate and the decisions it may take.

findings.name: Unit Mandate and Scope
findings.description: A unit's mandate states its reason for existence and the subject matter, geography, customer set or process it covers. W3C ORG offers org:purpose; CPOV types purpose as a code and suggests COFOG for public organisations, and adds spatial coverage of the administrative region an organisation covers. Mandate must trace to a delegating instrument, because ISO 37000 requires delegation to be formalized.

questions.text: What is the unit's stated remit, and is it expressed as free text, as codes from a governed scheme, or both?
Which instrument delegates this mandate to the unit, and from which higher authority or charter power does it derive?
Over which spatial, market, legal-entity or process scope does the mandate apply, and where does it explicitly not apply?
Does this mandate overlap or conflict with the remit of another unit, and which rule resolves the overlap?

data_elements.name: remitStatement
data_elements.description: Narrative statement of what the unit is mandated to do.

data_elements.name: purposeCode
data_elements.description: Coded purpose of the unit from a governed scheme (e.g. COFOG for public bodies).

data_elements.name: mandateValidity
data_elements.description: Period over which the mandate is in force.

data_elements.name: mandateScope
data_elements.description: Structured coverage of the mandate across spatial, market, entity and process dimensions.

artifacts.name: Delegation Instrument
artifacts.description: The formalized document or decision by which a governing body delegates a mandate to a unit, including the delegated scope, conditions and assurance arrangements.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the issuing body's decision reference; where absent, a Dimension-assigned ULID plus decision date (RFC 3339). Superseding instruments get new identifiers and point to the superseded one.

findings.name: Delegated Authority Limits
findings.description: Delegation is bounded: spend thresholds, contract-signing powers, hiring authority, approval tiers and escalation triggers. ISO 37000 holds that those who delegate remain accountable for the delegate's use of that authority, that delegation should be formalized together with appropriate assurance processes, and that no one should be accountable for matters over which they have no authority. Limits are therefore first-class data, not narrative.

questions.text: Which decision types may this unit take without escalation, and what quantitative or categorical limits bound each of them?
answer_data: limit value and unit of measure

questions.text: May the unit sub-delegate any part of its authority to a contained unit or post, and under what conditions?
Which assurance process verifies that delegated authority is being exercised within its limits, and at what cadence?
Under what circumstances is delegated authority suspended or withdrawn, and does withdrawal take effect immediately or at a stated date?

data_elements.name: authorityLimit
data_elements.description: A bounded decision right with type, quantitative limit and escalation threshold.

data_elements.name: limitAmount
data_elements.description: Monetary or numeric ceiling attached to a decision right, with unit of measure or currency.

data_elements.name: subDelegationRule
data_elements.description: Whether and how authority may be further delegated downward.

artifacts.name: Delegation of Authority Schedule
artifacts.description: The consolidated schedule mapping units to decision types, limits, escalation paths and assurance owners, used for both operation and audit.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the approving body's reference plus schedule version; each approved revision is a new serial instance with an effective date and a link to its predecessor.

layers.name: Accountability and Controls
layers.description: Who answers for a unit and which control constraints its structure must satisfy.

findings.name: Accountable Role for the Unit
findings.description: Each unit has a head or accountable role. W3C ORG models this as a Post or as a Membership linking an Agent, an Organization and a Role, which keeps the accountability slot stable while occupants change. ISO 37000 requires that decision-makers have appropriate authority, competence and resources for the responsibilities given. The person occupying the role is out of scope; the slot and its linkage are in scope.

questions.text: Which post or role is designated as head of the unit, and is that designation a property of the unit or of the post?
How is an acting, interim or vacant headship represented, and who holds the accountability while the slot is unfilled?
What evidence exists that the accountable role has the authority, competence and resources matching the unit's responsibilities?

data_elements.name: headPostRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the post (WM-ORG-004) designated as head of the unit.

data_elements.name: headshipState
data_elements.description: Whether the headship is substantively filled, acting, or vacant.

findings.inline_only_rationale: The accountable role is a typed reference into WM-ORG-004 plus a state code; the post description and appointment record are artifacts of the position and employment models, so producing a duplicate artifact here would fork the source of truth.

findings.name: Segregation of Duties and Structural Controls
findings.description: Structure itself carries control obligations: certain functions must not report into the unit they oversee, incompatible mandates must not sit in one unit, and control functions may require an independent line to a governing body. ISO 37000 frames this through accountability that cannot be discharged without matching authority and through formalized delegation with assurance. Violations are structural defects detectable at graph level.

questions.text: Which pairs or sets of mandates must never be held by the same unit, and which rule set encodes that prohibition?
Which units require an independent reporting line that bypasses their operational parent, and to which body does that line run?
How are segregation violations detected when a reorganization is proposed, and does detection block the change or only warn?
Under what conditions may a segregation rule be waived, who may approve the waiver, and for how long?

data_elements.name: segregationRuleRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a structural control rule applying to the unit.

data_elements.name: requiresIndependentLine
data_elements.description: Whether the unit must report independently of its operational parent.

data_elements.name: segregationWaiver
data_elements.description: An approved, time-bounded exception to a structural control rule with its compensating control.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Control rules are governed by a policy or compliance model and referenced here; evaluation results surface in the structure validation report artifact rather than as a distinct artifact class.

bundles.name: Establishment and Staffing
bundles.description: The posts a unit is authorized to carry and the staffing actually measured in it.
bundles.rationale: org:Post exists independently of its holder, which makes authorized establishment a unit-side fact distinct from employment. ESRS S1-6 and human-capital reporting practice require dated, methodologically declared headcount and FTE figures, so measurement must be separated from plan.

layers.name: Establishment Plan
layers.description: The authorized complement of posts seated in a unit.

findings.name: Authorized Post Complement
findings.description: The establishment is the set of posts a unit is authorized to carry, independent of whether they are filled. W3C ORG's Post 'exists independently of who fills it', which is exactly what makes an establishment countable. This model records the authorization, its approving instrument, the count and its budget linkage; the post's own definition belongs to WM-ORG-004.

questions.text: How many posts is the unit authorized to carry, expressed as post count and as budgeted full-time equivalents?
Who may increase or decrease the establishment, and does a change require a reorganization act or only a budget decision?
Which specific posts (WM-ORG-004) are seated in this unit, and can a post be seated in more than one unit at once?
What is the tolerated variance between authorized establishment and actual staffing before escalation is triggered?

data_elements.name: authorizedPostCount
data_elements.description: Number of posts the unit is authorized to carry.

data_elements.name: authorizedFte
data_elements.description: Budgeted full-time-equivalent capacity of the unit for a stated period.

data_elements.name: seatedPostRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a post seated in the unit, with validity period.

data_elements.name: costCentreCode
data_elements.description: Cost centre code associated with the unit for budget attribution, as surfaced by SCIM costCenter.

artifacts.name: Establishment Table
artifacts.description: The approved table of authorized posts per unit with counts, FTE, cost centre linkage and the instrument that approved each line.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by organization identifier plus budget or establishment period plus version; each approved revision is a new serial instance with effective date and predecessor link.

findings.name: Unit-Level Occupancy State
findings.description: At unit granularity the relevant facts are how many authorized posts are filled, vacant, frozen or over-established, and since when. Individual occupancy is an employment fact about a named person and is excluded; the aggregate is a unit fact. Keeping only the aggregate here is what makes structure data disclosable without touching personal data.

questions.text: How many authorized posts in this unit are currently filled, vacant, frozen or in notice period, and as of which instant?
Is the unit carrying more filled posts than authorized, and under which approved exception?
Is occupancy asserted directly on the unit or derived from employment records, and which is authoritative when they disagree?

data_elements.name: filledPostCount
data_elements.description: Number of authorized posts currently occupied, as of a stated instant.

data_elements.name: vacantPostCount
data_elements.description: Number of authorized posts currently unoccupied.

data_elements.name: occupancyAsOf
data_elements.description: The instant to which occupancy counts refer.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Unit-level occupancy is a derived aggregate over employment and position records; publishing it as its own artifact would create a second, drifting source of truth. It is carried inline on the unit and materialised only inside the headcount snapshot artifact.

layers.name: Staffing Measurement
layers.description: Dated, method-declared measurement of staffing attributed to a unit, and the rules for disclosing it.

findings.name: Headcount and FTE Snapshot
findings.description: A staffing snapshot is a measurement event, not a unit attribute: it has an as-of date, a counting basis (head count or full-time equivalent, point-in-time or average over the period), a population definition and a preparer. ESRS S1-6 requires employee totals by head count and/or FTE with country and gender breakdowns and explicit methodology disclosure, which makes basis declaration mandatory rather than optional.

questions.text: Is the figure a head count or a full-time equivalent, and is it a point-in-time count at the reporting date or an average over the period?
Which worker categories are included - permanent, temporary, non-guaranteed hours, contingent, contractors - and which are excluded?
answer_data: treatment of shared or apportioned staff

questions.text: What is the difference between the snapshot's as-of date and the instant it was computed and ingested, and are both recorded?
Under what conditions is a prior snapshot restated rather than superseded, and how is the restatement flagged to consumers?

data_elements.name: headcountValue
data_elements.description: Measured staffing figure for the unit under a declared basis.

data_elements.name: countingBasis
data_elements.description: Declared counting basis and period convention for the figure.

data_elements.name: snapshotAsOfDate
data_elements.description: The date to which the measurement refers, distinct from when it was computed.

data_elements.name: observationTimestamp
data_elements.description: The instant the measurement was computed or ingested, in RFC 3339 form with explicit offset.

artifacts.name: Headcount Snapshot Series
artifacts.description: The dated series of staffing measurements per unit with basis, population definition, preparer and restatement flags, supporting trend analysis and external disclosure.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Each snapshot keyed by unit identifier plus as-of date plus basis code; the series itself keyed by organization identifier plus basis. Restatements are new instances that reference the superseded snapshot.

findings.name: Staffing Disclosure Thresholds
findings.description: Staffing figures for small units can identify individuals, so aggregation and suppression rules are part of the model, not of the consuming report. ESRS S1 itself uses thresholds, requiring country breakdowns only where an undertaking has 50 or more employees in a country and only for the ten largest countries, which demonstrates that threshold logic is normal in authoritative reporting standards.

questions.text: Below which cell size must a unit's staffing figure be suppressed or rolled up to its parent, and who sets that threshold?
Which breakdowns of staffing by unit are permitted for which audiences, and which combinations are prohibited because they enable re-identification?
How is the application of a suppression rule recorded so that a consumer can tell a suppressed value from a true zero?

data_elements.name: minimumCellSize
data_elements.description: Threshold below which unit-level staffing figures must not be published.

data_elements.name: suppressionApplied
data_elements.description: Marker distinguishing a suppressed value from a genuine zero.

data_elements.name: audienceClass
data_elements.description: Class of consumer for which a given breakdown is permitted.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Thresholds are policy parameters applied by the disclosure function; they are configuration on the access layer and on the headcount snapshot artifact rather than an artifact in their own right.

bundles.name: Change and Time
bundles.description: How structure changes, what evidences the change, and how any past state can be reconstructed.
bundles.rationale: org:ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultingOrganization gives n:m restructuring lineage; ROR tombstones withdrawn records and retains relationships; IFRS 8 requires restatement or disclosure when internal structure changes. Change and time therefore need dedicated, event-based treatment.

layers.name: Structural Change Events
layers.description: The acts that create, alter, combine, move or end units, and the lineage they produce.

findings.name: Reorganization Act
findings.description: A reorganization act is a decision that reshapes structure. It carries at least three distinct times - when it was decided, when it takes effect in the world, and when it was recorded - plus the deciding authority, the affected units and the change kind. W3C ORG's ChangeEvent 'resulted in a major change to an organization such as a merger or complete restructuring'; IFRS 8 then requires prior-period segment information to be restated or the change disclosed, so an act has consequences outside this model.

questions.text: What kind of act is this - establish, rename, reclassify, reparent, merge, split, transfer between organizations, or disband - and which units does it affect in which role?
What are the decision instant, the effective instant and the record instant of this act, each with an explicit offset?
Which body took the decision, under which delegated power, and is the decision instrument attached as evidence?
Which downstream obligations does the act trigger - segment restatement, employee information and consultation, directory reprovisioning, contract novation?
May an act be recorded with an effective date in the past, and what compensating controls apply to retroactive entries?

data_elements.name: reorganizationActKind
data_elements.description: Coded kind of structural change.

data_elements.name: decisionTimestamp
data_elements.description: When the decision was taken, in RFC 3339 form with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: effectiveTimestamp
data_elements.description: When the change takes effect in the world.

data_elements.name: recordedTimestamp
data_elements.description: When the change was captured in the record, kept separate from event time.

data_elements.name: affectedUnits
data_elements.description: Units affected by the act with their role as original or resulting participant.

artifacts.name: Reorganization Decision Record
artifacts.description: The evidenced record of one structural change act: decision instrument, authority, affected units and roles, the three timestamps, and the list of triggered downstream obligations.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the deciding body's official decision reference where one exists; otherwise a Dimension-assigned ULID. Never keyed by date alone, since several acts may share a date.

findings.name: Unit Lineage and Succession
findings.description: Merges and splits create many-to-many lineage that a simple parent pointer cannot express. W3C ORG uses originalOrganization and resultingOrganization on a ChangeEvent; ROR uses predecessor and successor relationships and keeps relationships on inactive or withdrawn records as historical tombstones. Lineage must survive the disappearance of its endpoints so that historical references still resolve.

questions.text: Which units are the predecessors and successors of this unit, and through which act was each lineage edge created?
Does a merged or renamed unit retain its identifier as a continuation, or is a new identifier minted with a lineage edge to the old one?
When a consumer dereferences the identifier of a disbanded unit, what is returned - a tombstone, a redirect to the successor, or an error?
When only part of a unit moves in a split, how is the partial transfer of establishment, mandate and staffing apportioned across the lineage edge?

data_elements.name: predecessorUnitRefs
data_elements.description: Units from which this unit derives through a change act.

data_elements.name: successorUnitRefs
data_elements.description: Units into which this unit continues after a change act.

data_elements.name: lineageActRef
data_elements.description: Reference to the reorganization act that created the lineage edge.

artifacts.name: Unit Lineage Graph
artifacts.description: The directed acyclic graph of predecessor and successor edges across all acts, including tombstoned nodes, used to resolve historical unit references.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by organization identifier; nodes keyed by unitIdentifier including retired ones, edges keyed by the act reference that created them.

layers.name: Temporal Validity
layers.description: Effective dating, bitemporality and reconstruction of the structure at any past instant.

findings.name: Effective Dating and Bitemporality
findings.description: Every structural assertion - membership in a hierarchy, a reporting line, a mandate, an establishment line - carries a validity period in world time and a separate transaction period in record time. RFC 3339 requires a stated relationship to UTC and offers '-00:00' where the instant is known but the local offset is not, a distinction that matters for multinational effective dates. ROR's admin block separates created from last_modified, illustrating the record-time axis in practice.

questions.text: What are the validity start and end of this assertion in world time, and is an open-ended end represented explicitly or by absence?
When was this assertion first recorded and when was it last modified or superseded in the record, independently of its world-time validity?
Which time offset is used for effective dates in a multi-jurisdiction organization, and is a legal local midnight or a UTC instant intended?
Are gaps or overlaps permitted in the validity of successive parent assignments for the same unit and hierarchy?

data_elements.name: validFrom
data_elements.description: Start of world-time validity for a structural assertion, RFC 3339 with explicit offset.

data_elements.name: validTo
data_elements.description: End of world-time validity, absent or explicitly open where still current.

data_elements.name: recordedFrom
data_elements.description: Start of record-time validity, i.e. when the system first held this assertion.

data_elements.name: temporalGranularity
data_elements.description: Whether the assertion is dated to an instant or to a legal calendar day in a stated jurisdiction.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Bitemporal stamps are per-assertion attributes that must travel with every edge and record; isolating them into an artifact would detach them from the assertions they qualify.

findings.name: As-Of Reconstruction and Versioning
findings.description: Consumers need the structure as it stood at a past instant, both as it actually was (world time) and as it was believed to be at the time (record time). IFRS 8's requirement to restate prior-period segment information after an internal reorganization, or otherwise disclose the change, makes exact historical reconstruction an external obligation rather than a convenience. Reconstruction outputs must be reproducible and identified.

questions.text: Given a world-time instant and a record-time instant, can the full unit set, hierarchy and reporting lines be reproduced deterministically?
How is a structure version identified so that two consumers can prove they are looking at the same state?
Does the model support producing both the pre-reorganization and post-reorganization views of a prior period for comparative reporting?
answer_data: mapping between old and new units

questions.text: How far back is full reconstruction guaranteed, and what happens to reconstruction after retention-driven deletion?

data_elements.name: structureVersionId
data_elements.description: Identifier of a reproducible structure state.

data_elements.name: contentDigest
data_elements.description: Cryptographic digest over the canonical serialisation of the structure state.

data_elements.name: asOfParameters
data_elements.description: The world-time and record-time instants that parameterise a reconstruction.

artifacts.name: Structure As-Of View
artifacts.description: A frozen, digest-identified export of the complete unit set, hierarchies, reporting lines and mandates valid at a stated world-time and record-time pair.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by structureVersionId plus the as-of pair; content digest is the integrity anchor. Dates alone are never used as the identifier.

bundles.name: Governance, Provenance and Disclosure
bundles.description: Who owns the structure record, what evidences it, how long it is kept, and who may see what.
bundles.rationale: The parent organization, not a registrar, governs unit structure, so authority, evidence, retention and disclosure must be modelled explicitly. NARA shows disposition authority as a mandatory governed instrument, and ESRS shows external disclosure obligations acting on the same data.

layers.name: Provenance and Record Authority
layers.description: Which system and which body are authoritative for each structural assertion, and what evidences it.

findings.name: Record Authority and Source of Truth
findings.description: Unit structure has no external registrar: the parent organization is the sole authority, unlike legal identity where GLEIF and business registers verify against authoritative local sources. Different attributes may nonetheless have different masters - HR for establishment, finance for cost centres, governance secretariat for mandates - so authority is asserted per attribute group, with a declared conflict resolution order.

questions.text: For each attribute group - identity, hierarchy, mandate, establishment, staffing - which system and which role is the master?
When two systems assert different values for the same attribute, which precedence order applies and who adjudicates a persistent conflict?
Is any part of the structure externally verifiable (a registered branch, a statutory committee), and against which register?
For an ingested assertion, what are the source system, extraction instant and transformation applied before it reached this model?

data_elements.name: masterSystemRef
data_elements.description: The authoritative system for a given attribute group of the unit.

data_elements.name: recordOwnerRole
data_elements.description: The role accountable for the correctness of the structure record.

data_elements.name: ingestionTimestamp
data_elements.description: When an externally sourced assertion was ingested, kept separate from its event time.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Record authority is metadata attached to each assertion and to the model's stewardship entry in the S1 model; a separate artifact would duplicate the stewardship register that already governs ownership.

findings.name: Evidence and Structural Validation
findings.description: A structural claim is only operable if it can be checked. Validation covers referential integrity against WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, acyclicity per hierarchy, temporal consistency, establishment-versus-actual variance, segregation rules and the FHIR-style minimum that an entry must have at least one name or identifier. Results are evidence, with severity and an owner, not silent failures.

questions.text: Which validation rules apply to a unit record, at which severity, and which of them block a write?
What is the minimum viable unit record that may be persisted, and does it require at least one name or identifier?
Which assertions require attached documentary evidence before they are treated as authoritative rather than provisional?
Which quality measures are tracked over the structure graph - orphan rate, stale-record age, unmandated units, over-establishment - and what are their thresholds?

data_elements.name: validationRule
data_elements.description: A named, expressible constraint over the structure graph with severity.

data_elements.name: validationResult
data_elements.description: Outcome of evaluating a rule against a unit or the graph, with instant and severity.

data_elements.name: evidenceRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a document or record substantiating an assertion.

artifacts.name: Structure Validation Report
artifacts.description: Dated report of all rule evaluations over a structure version, listing failures with severity, affected units, owner and remediation state.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by structureVersionId plus evaluation instant (RFC 3339) plus rule set version; reports are immutable once issued.

layers.name: Access, Disclosure and Retention
layers.description: Controlled release of structure information and its governed disposition.

findings.name: Structure Disclosure and Privacy
findings.description: Structure data spans public facts (a published org chart of a public authority under CPOV-style transparency) and sensitive facts (unfilled posts signalling a planned restructuring, or small-unit staffing that identifies individuals). Disclosure is therefore scoped per projection and per audience, and small-cell staffing must be suppressed or aggregated before release.

questions.text: Which disclosure classes exist for structure data - public, counterparty, auditor, internal, restricted - and which fields belong to each?
Which structure fields can identify a natural person, directly or by combination, and what safeguard applies to each?
Which structural changes are embargoed until announcement, and what is the release trigger and the holder of the embargo?
Where employee information and consultation duties apply before a reorganization takes effect, how is that dependency represented as a precondition on the act?

data_elements.name: disclosureClass
data_elements.description: Classification governing who may receive a structure field or projection.

data_elements.name: embargoedUntil
data_elements.description: Instant before which a structural change must not be disclosed.

data_elements.name: consultationEvidenceRef
data_elements.description: Evidence that a required employee information or consultation step was completed.

artifacts.name: Structure Disclosure Package
artifacts.description: A scoped, audience-specific release of structure information with suppression rules applied, listing exactly which fields were included, redacted and suppressed.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by structureVersionId plus disclosure class plus release instant (RFC 3339); the redaction manifest digest binds the package to the rules that produced it.

findings.name: Retention and Disposition
findings.description: Structure records have long evidential value: lineage must outlive the units it links, because historical references keep resolving. Retention should follow a governed disposition authority rather than ad hoc deletion - NARA's model is that use of the General Records Schedules 'is mandatory' and agencies must justify any agency-specific schedule. Deletion must be reconciled with the bitemporal reconstruction guarantee.

questions.text: Which disposition authority or retention schedule governs each class of structure record, and who approved it?
Which structure records are permanent or archival - founding acts, lineage edges, mandate instruments - and which are transitory?
How is deletion of a unit record reconciled with the need to keep lineage edges resolvable for historical references?
How does a legal hold suspend disposition for affected structure records, and how is the hold released and evidenced?

data_elements.name: retentionClass
data_elements.description: Record class determining the applicable retention period and disposition action.

data_elements.name: dispositionAction
data_elements.description: Action at end of retention: destroy, transfer to archive, or review.

data_elements.name: legalHoldRef
data_elements.description: Reference to a hold suspending disposition for the record.

artifacts.name: Structure Disposition Schedule
artifacts.description: The approved schedule binding each class of structure record to a retention period, disposition action and appraisal rationale, including permanent classes such as founding acts and lineage.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Identified by the approving records authority's schedule reference plus version; supersession is recorded explicitly rather than by overwrite.

layers.name: External Alignment
layers.description: Mapping to external vocabularies and controlling fidelity loss on export.

findings.name: Standards Crosswalk
findings.description: The unit maps outward to org:OrganizationalUnit with org:unitOf/org:subOrganizationOf, to CPOV hasUnit for public bodies, to a FHIR Organization with partOf and type, to LDAP organizationalUnit with ou, to SCIM department/division, to schema.org department/parentOrganization with iso6523Code, and to an ISO/IEC 6523 ICD plus organization part identifier for e-business addressing. Each mapping is an alignment claim with a direction and a fidelity note, never a conformance claim.

questions.text: For each external target vocabulary, which local element maps to which term, in which direction, and with what cardinality mismatch?
Is a conformance claim being made against any target, and if so what evidence - a passing test suite or a validation profile - supports it?
Where do target vocabularies disagree with this model - for instance schema.org conflating department with subsidiary, or FHIR having no distinct unit class - and how is the disagreement recorded?
How are target vocabulary version changes detected, and what is the review cadence for the crosswalk?

data_elements.name: crosswalkEntry
data_elements.description: One directional mapping between a local element and an external term, with fidelity note.

data_elements.name: targetVocabularyVersion
data_elements.description: The exact version of the external vocabulary the mapping was validated against.

data_elements.name: conformanceClaim
data_elements.description: Explicit statement of whether conformance is claimed and on what evidence.

artifacts.name: Crosswalk Map
artifacts.description: Machine-readable mapping table from this model's elements to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 terms, with direction, fidelity notes and target versions.
artifacts.identity_strategy: Keyed by model version plus target vocabulary identifier plus target version; a new target version produces a new serial mapping instance.

findings.name: Projection Fidelity and Lossy Export
findings.description: Exports lose information in predictable ways: LDAP 'ou' and SCIM 'department' carry only names, so identifier, kind, validity period, mandate and reporting type vanish; org charts drop mandate and staffing; segment reports aggregate units away. A projection must declare what it drops and must never be re-imported as authoritative, or the lossy copy will silently overwrite the governed record.

questions.text: For each defined projection, which elements are omitted, flattened or aggregated, and is that loss declared to consumers?
May any projection be re-imported as a source of truth, and what guard prevents an accidental round-trip overwrite?
How stale may a projection be before consumers must be warned, and how is its generation instant and source version published with it?

data_elements.name: projectionName
data_elements.description: Identifier of a defined outward view over the structure.

data_elements.name: lossManifest
data_elements.description: Declared list of elements omitted, flattened or aggregated by a projection.

data_elements.name: sourceStructureVersion
data_elements.description: The structure version a projection was generated from.

findings.inline_only_rationale: Projections are realised by the org chart, reporting matrix, as-of view and disclosure package artifacts already defined; this finding governs their fidelity metadata rather than producing a further artifact.

functions.name: Resolve Unit Identity
functions.description: Resolve any inbound reference - master-system identifier, ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identifier, alias, former name, LDAP distinguished name or IdP group id - to the single current unit record or to a tombstone with a successor pointer.
preconditions: The unit register is loaded for the stated parent organization
The alias and lineage indexes cover the requested as-of instant
effects: Emits a resolution audit entry with the input, method and outcome
Never mutates the unit record

functions.name: Validate Structure Graph
functions.description: Evaluate integrity rules over a structure version: acyclicity within each named hierarchy, single parent per hierarchy per validity interval, no orphans, referential integrity to WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, temporal gap and overlap rules, and segregation-of-duties constraints.
outputs: validation result set with severity per finding
preconditions: The structure version is fully materialised and immutable
The rule set version is published and resolvable
effects: Produces a Structure Validation Report artifact
May block a pending write when blocking failures are present

functions.name: Reconstruct Structure As Of
functions.description: Return the unit set, hierarchies, reporting lines and mandates valid at a given world-time instant as recorded at a given record-time instant, producing a deterministic, digest-identified view.
outputs: Structure As-Of View with structureVersionId and content digest
list of elements excluded by disclosure class
preconditions: Bitemporal stamps exist on all included assertions
The requested instants fall inside the reconstruction horizon
effects: Materialises a frozen, immutable as-of export
Records the query parameters and digest for reproducibility

functions.name: Apply Reorganization Act
functions.description: Apply an evidenced structural change - establish, rename, reclassify, reparent, merge, split, transfer or disband - creating lineage edges, closing and opening validity intervals, and registering downstream obligations.
inputs: reorganization act record with kind and affected units
outputs: updated unit records with closed and opened validity intervals
preconditions: The deciding body holds the delegated authority for the act kind
Pre-commit validation passes or an approved override exists
Any jurisdictional consultation precondition is evidenced as complete
effects: Mutates the structure graph as of the effective instant
Produces a Reorganization Decision Record artifact
Notifies segment reporting, directory provisioning and contract owners

functions.name: Derive Org Chart Projection
functions.description: Generate a hierarchy view for a named hierarchy at an as-of instant, containing unit names and kinds only, with mandate detail and staffing deliberately excluded.
preconditions: The named hierarchy exists and has valid edges at the as-of instant
The requesting principal holds read scope for the hierarchy
effects: Emits a serial projection instance bound to its source structure version
Marks the output as non-authoritative and non-reimportable

functions.name: Evaluate Mandate Conflict
functions.description: Detect overlapping or incompatible remits across units and breaches of authority limits or independence requirements, before or after a proposed structural change.
outputs: conflict findings with affected units and rule references
preconditions: Mandates are expressed with structured scope, not narrative only
The rule set encodes incompatible mandate pairs
effects: Records conflicts as validation findings with severity
Triggers a waiver workflow when an exception is sought

functions.name: Compute Headcount Rollup
functions.description: Aggregate staffing measurements up a named hierarchy under a declared counting basis and period convention, applying suppression where a cell falls below the minimum size.
outputs: rolled-up figures per unit with basis and period stated
suppression markers distinguishing suppressed values from true zeros
preconditions: Underlying snapshots share a compatible basis and population definition
The minimum cell size policy is resolved for the audience
effects: Appends to the Headcount Snapshot Series artifact
Logs each suppression with the rule applied

functions.name: Reconcile External Directory
functions.description: Compare LDAP or SCIM representations of units against the governed structure, report drift, and push corrections outward without ever accepting the directory as a source of truth.
inputs: directory export (LDAP entries or SCIM Groups and Enterprise User attributes)
outputs: drift report of name, membership and hierarchy differences
preconditions: A mapping from unit identifiers to directory distinguished names or group ids exists
The directory export carries a generation timestamp
effects: Never mutates the governed structure from directory content
Queues outbound provisioning changes and records unresolved name-only matches

functions.name: Emit Standards Mapping
functions.description: Serialise the structure into a target vocabulary - W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR Organization, schema.org, or an ISO/IEC 6523 party identifier - using the versioned crosswalk and attaching a fidelity declaration.
preconditions: A crosswalk entry exists for every included element and target version
No conformance claim is asserted without a referenced test result
effects: Produces a serial export bound to the crosswalk version used
Records any element dropped for lack of a target term

functions.name: Apply Disposition
functions.description: Execute the approved retention schedule over structure records: destroy, transfer to archive or flag for review, while preserving the tombstones and lineage edges required for historical reference resolution.
outputs: list of records retained under hold or as permanent
preconditions: A governed disposition authority covers every record class in scope
No legal hold applies to the record
Tombstone and lineage minimums are defined
effects: Irreversibly removes or transfers eligible records
Reduces the reconstruction horizon and records the new horizon
Preserves lineage edges and tombstones for resolvability

composition.purpose: Every unit resolves to exactly one parent organization, which holds legal identity, registration and external identifiers. W3C ORG grounds the dependency: a unit 'only has full recognition within the context of that Organization'.

Units contain or govern established posts. This model holds the establishment count, seating and unit-level occupancy; the post as an object that 'exists independently of who fills it' is defined in WM-ORG-004.
Employment records fill the posts seated in a unit and are the derivation source for unit-level occupancy counts; persons and contracts never enter this model.
Unit mandates trace upward to powers held by the organization; ISO 37000 requires delegation to be formalized and delegators to remain accountable, so the upstream power must be resolvable.

A unit may be associated with one or more premises, but FHIR keeps Location distinct from Organization and Eurostat's local unit is a geographic statistical construct, so premises are referenced rather than embedded.
The parent organization owns the structure record and units have no independent standing; ownership, custodianship and accountability facets come from the stewardship model.
Disclosure classes defined here are enforced by grants issued in the access model; this model supplies the scoped projections and suppression parameters, not the grant machinery.
Reorganization acts, mandate changes, waivers and disposition actions require immutable audit facets with separate event and record timestamps.

Primary structural alignment for OrganizationalUnit, hasUnit/unitOf, subOrganizationOf, purpose, classification, Post, Site and ChangeEvent. Unit-to-unit reportsTo is declared an extension, since org:reportsTo binds Agents and Posts.
Public-sector profile alignment for hasUnit, code-valued purpose (COFOG), classification and spatial coverage; applicable only where the parent organization is a public body.

Healthcare-sector projection where departments are Organization instances chained by partOf and non-hierarchical relations use OrganizationAffiliation; a known structural conflict with the distinct-unit-class model.

composition.target: ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification (via Peppol ICD registry)
composition.purpose: External addressing of a unit as an organization part under the parent's ICD and organization identifier, used for e-business party and delivery-location identification.
Outbound-only projection targets. Both carry unit information as names without identifiers, validity or typed edges, so alignment is declared lossy and re-import is prohibited.
Mapping of internal units to enterprise, kind-of-activity unit and local unit for statistical reporting, recorded as a derivation with explicit boundary mismatch rather than as equivalence.

The internal reporting hierarchy is an input to segment identification under the management approach, and reorganization acts trigger the restate-or-disclose obligation; segment determination itself stays outside this model.

owner_package_requirements: The adopting Dimension must name a single parent organization as owner of every unit record; units have no independent standing and cannot own their own structure entry.

The Dimension must declare, per attribute group (identity, hierarchy, mandate, establishment, staffing), which system is master and publish the precedence order used to resolve conflicting assertions.
The Dimension must publish a governed unit-kind code list, a status vocabulary and a named hierarchy inventory before any unit record is accepted.
The Dimension must bind every structure record class to an approved disposition authority and declare its bitemporal reconstruction horizon.
The Dimension must declare its minimum cell size for staffing disclosure and the audience classes to which each projection may be released.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Use a Dimension-scoped namespace of the form <dimension-namespace>/org-unit/ with unit identifiers qualified by the parent organization identifier, since unit identifiers are only unique inside their parent. Do not mint global IRIs implying registry status: ROR and GLEIF do not identify internal subdivisions. Where external addressing is needed, compose an ISO/IEC 6523 triple (ICD:organizationIdentifier:organizationPartIdentifier) rather than inventing a new global scheme. Keep hierarchy, reporting-line and mandate edge types in distinct sub-namespaces so that concurrent hierarchies remain separable.
