canonicalization_rules: Serialise timestamps as RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or 'Z'; use '-00:00' only where the UTC instant is known but the local offset is not.
Order collections deterministically before digesting: units by unitIdentifier, edges by (hierarchyIdentifier, parent, child, validFrom), aliases by (type, language, validFrom).
Normalise names with Unicode NFC and preserve original casing and script; never fold case for identity purposes.
Represent open-ended validity by an explicit open marker rather than by a sentinel far-future date, so that digests do not change when conventions change.
Exclude derived elements (hierarchyPath, rollup counts, projections) from the canonical form; recompute them from asserted edges.
patch_rules: Correcting a mistaken record and recording a real-world change are different operations: corrections adjust record time only, reorganizations open and close world-time intervals.
A reorganization patch must carry decision, effective and record timestamps and must reference the deciding authority; a patch missing any of the three is rejected.
Patches are additive over the bitemporal store: no assertion is overwritten in place, and superseded intervals remain retrievable until disposition.
Identifier fields, lineage edges and issued artifacts are immutable; changing them requires a new record with an explicit supersession edge.
Backdated patches beyond the declared window require named approval and are marked so consumers can detect retroactive change.
compatibility_rules: Adding an optional element, a new named hierarchy or a new code value is a minor change; removing an element, tightening cardinality or retiring a code value is a major change.
Retired unit-kind and status codes are deprecated with a successor mapping and never removed from the published code list.
Crosswalk entries are versioned against an exact target vocabulary version; a target version bump requires a new crosswalk instance and a review, not an in-place edit.

Conformance to an external standard is asserted only with a referenced test result; where a target lacks a term (for example unit-to-unit reportsTo in W3C ORG), the export declares non-conformance rather than silently coercing.
Projections never round-trip: a consumer may not submit an org chart, LDAP or SCIM export back as a source of truth.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier assigned by the parent organization (unit register key, official decision reference, approved schedule reference).

Governed global identifier or IRI where one genuinely exists - an ISO/IEC 6523 ICD plus organization identifier plus organization part identifier, or an LEI where the subdivision is itself a registered legal entity.
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, with the minting act recorded, used only when neither of the above exists.
A date, a name, an org-chart position or a cost centre code is never an identifier; at most they are qualifiers on an identifier.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values use RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit UTC offset or 'Z'. Event time (decision instant, effective instant, snapshot as-of date) and observation time (computation, ingestion, record instant) are recorded as separate fields and never conflated; '-00:00' is reserved for a known UTC instant with unknown local offset.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts are named <artifact-id>--<scope-key>--<as-of or effective instant in RFC 3339 basic form>--v<sequence>, where scope-key is the organization identifier plus any hierarchy, basis or target-vocabulary qualifier. The instant qualifies but never replaces the identifier, and the sequence disambiguates multiple instances sharing an instant.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every issued artifact carries a content digest over its canonical serialisation, the structureVersionId it was derived from, the rule-set or crosswalk version applied, and its loss manifest where it is a projection. Issued artifacts are immutable: corrections are new serial instances that reference the superseded one, and any artifact whose digest does not verify is treated as unusable rather than as merely stale.

policies: The parent organization is the sole authority for unit structure; no downstream system, directory or projection may originate or overwrite a structural assertion.
Reorganization is an evidenced act, not an attribute edit: every change to existence, parentage, kind or mandate requires a decision record with authority, evidence and three distinct timestamps.
Unit-level staffing is published only above the declared minimum cell size, with suppression markers distinguishing suppressed values from true zeros.
Delegated authority must be formalized with stated limits and an assurance process, and no unit may be held accountable for matters over which it holds no authority.
Lineage edges and tombstones outlive the units they connect, so that historical references remain resolvable after disbandment.
External standard mappings are alignments; conformance is claimed only with referenced test evidence, and known conflicts are published with the mapping.

read: Read the current unit record, its hierarchy position and its reporting lines within the requester's disclosure class.
Reconstruct any past structure state by world-time and record-time instant within the declared reconstruction horizon.
Read mandate, authority limits and establishment only with the corresponding scope; staffing figures only above the minimum cell size.
Resolve an alias, former name or external identifier to the current unit or to a tombstone with a successor pointer.
create: Create a unit only with a parent organization reference, at least one name or identifier, a kind code from the governed list and an effective instant.
Create a reorganization act with kind, affected units and roles, deciding authority, evidence reference and decision, effective and record timestamps.
Create a headcount snapshot only with a declared counting basis, population definition, as-of date and observation timestamp.
Create a mandate only with a resolvable delegating instrument and a validity period.
update: Update names, aliases and contact-style attributes directly, with record-time versioning and an actor reference.
Change existence, parentage, kind or mandate only through a reorganization act; direct edits to those fields are rejected.
Correct erroneous records through a record-time correction that preserves the prior belief rather than overwriting it.
Supersede an establishment table, authority schedule or disposition schedule by issuing a new version with an explicit predecessor link.
delete: Do not delete units to represent cessation: disband them through an act and retain the tombstone with lineage edges intact.
Withdraw records created in error using the withdrawn status with a reason, keeping the distinction from real-world cessation.
Destroy or transfer structure records only under an approved disposition authority, with no active legal hold, recording the action per record.
After disposition, publish the reduced reconstruction horizon and retain the minimum tombstone fields needed for reference resolution.

roles.name: Structure Owner (parent organization governing body)
responsibilities: Holds ultimate accountability for the structure record and approves the delegation of authority schedule.
Approves reorganization acts that create, merge, transfer or disband units.
Resolves persistent conflicts between attribute masters.

roles.name: Structure Steward
responsibilities: Maintains the unit register, the kind code list, the status vocabulary and the named hierarchy inventory.
Applies reorganization acts, opens and closes validity intervals and maintains lineage edges.
Runs validation, triages findings and tracks remediation to closure.

roles.name: Mandate and Delegation Custodian
responsibilities: Records mandates and authority limits against their delegating instruments and assurance processes.
Detects overlapping remits and segregation-of-duties breaches and manages time-bounded waivers.
Reviews delegation formalisation before a reorganization act is approved.

roles.name: Workforce Data Custodian
responsibilities: Defines counting bases and population definitions and produces dated headcount and FTE snapshots.
Reconciles authorized establishment against actual staffing and escalates variance breaches.
Applies minimum cell size suppression and logs each suppression decision.

roles.name: Records and Disclosure Officer
responsibilities: Binds record classes to an approved disposition authority and executes disposition under legal-hold checks.
Approves disclosure packages, embargoes and audience-specific projections.
Maintains the redaction manifest and the reconstruction horizon statement.

roles.name: Interoperability Custodian
responsibilities: Maintains crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523 with exact target versions.
Monitors target vocabulary version drift and schedules crosswalk reviews.
Guards against projection round-trips and publishes loss manifests with every export.

access.default_rule: Deny by default. A principal receives only the elements permitted by its disclosure class for the requested scope; unit identity, name, kind and containment position are the widest normally granted set, while mandate detail, authority limits, establishment and staffing require additional explicit scope.
exceptions: Public authorities may be obliged to publish their unit structure and purpose, so a public disclosure class may expose identity, name, kind, purpose and hierarchy without individual grant.
Auditors and assurance providers receive read access to mandate, authority limits and validation reports for a bounded engagement period without staffing detail below the minimum cell size.
Embargoed reorganization acts are withheld from all classes except the deciding body and named preparers until the release trigger, even from principals who otherwise hold structure read scope.
Employee representative bodies may receive advance access to a proposed reorganization where a jurisdictional information and consultation duty applies, ahead of general disclosure.
Emergency break-glass read of full structure requires named approval, is time-boxed, and is reported to the Structure Owner after the fact.
audit_requirements: Log every read of mandate, authority limit, establishment and staffing elements with principal, scope, purpose and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Log every reorganization act application with the three timestamps, deciding authority, evidence reference and validation verdict.
Log every suppression, redaction and embargo decision with the rule applied, so a consumer can distinguish suppression from absence.
Log every disposition action with the schedule reference, hold check outcome and the resulting reconstruction horizon.
Retain audit entries under the same disposition authority as the records they describe and never below the reconstruction horizon.

read_order: AGENTS.md - identify the model, its type and the four resolvable URLs before any other action
Specification URL - read scope, boundaries and the bundle/layer/finding structure to learn what this model does and does not own
Storage type URL - learn the concrete projection (JSON, YAML, Markdown, Git, MongoDB or other) and the canonicalization rules; treat the projection as non-semantic
Interface URL - learn the read, create, update and delete operations, their scopes and the deny-by-default access rule
Processes URL - learn the reorganization, validation, snapshot, disclosure and disposition procedures and their preconditions
Governed code lists and hierarchy inventory - resolve unit kinds, status vocabulary and named hierarchies before writing any record
Crosswalk map - consult before emitting to any external vocabulary and honour the declared fidelity and non-conformance notes

coverage.claim: This model covers the internal structure of an organization to a depth that is defensible from primary standards: unit identity and classification, containment and reporting relations, mandate and delegated authority, establishment and measured staffing, evidenced structural change with bitemporal validity, and the provenance, retention, disclosure and interoperability rules needed to operate it. It is grounded chiefly in W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR R5, IETF schema and timestamp standards, ISO/IEC 6523 addressing as deployed by Peppol, IFRS 8, ESRS S1, ISO 37000 governance guidance and NARA disposition practice. It makes no claim to universal or metaphysical completeness, and several structural nodes rest on interpretation rather than a normative requirement, which is recorded below.

checklist.notes: Parent-scoped master identifiers are treated as primary; ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification supplies the external addressing slot; UUID/ULID is the explicit fallback. Grounded in W3C ORG, Peppol's ICD registry and schema.org iso6523Code. Falsified the assumption of a global unit registry using ROR's stated scope exclusion and GLEIF's legal-entity-only remit.

Status vocabulary separates operating, ceased and created-in-error following ROR's active/inactive/withdrawn distinction; transitions requiring a reorganization act are distinguished from corrections; tombstoning is mandated so lineage outlives units.

Containment, concurrent hierarchies, reporting lines and non-hierarchical affiliations are separated, following W3C ORG's split of hasUnit/subOrganizationOf from reportsTo and FHIR's split of partOf from OrganizationAffiliation. Unit-to-unit reporting is flagged as an extension, not conformant use.

Bitemporality is mandatory: world-time validity and record-time transaction intervals on every assertion; decision, effective and record instants on every act; RFC 3339 with explicit offset and the '-00:00' unknown-offset convention. As-of reconstruction is tied to IFRS 8's restate-or-disclose obligation.

Per-attribute-group master systems with a declared precedence order, ingestion timestamps separate from event time, evidence attachment requirements for authoritative assertions, and lineage edges carrying the act that created them.

The parent organization is the sole owner; units have no independent standing. Accountable role modelled as a post/role slot rather than a person, and ISO 37000's rule that delegators remain accountable is carried into the authority-limit finding.

Explicit rule classes: acyclicity per hierarchy, single parent per hierarchy per interval, referential integrity to WM-ORG-001 and WM-ORG-004, gap/overlap policy, FHIR's name-or-identifier minimum, and segregation constraints. Results are issued as an immutable report artifact with severity and blocking semantics.

Deny by default with bundle/layer/finding/artifact scopes; disclosure classes per projection; embargo on unannounced reorganization; break-glass is time-boxed and reported. Public-authority transparency is handled as a declared exception rather than as the default.

Disposition follows an approved authority on the NARA model where schedule use is mandatory; permanent classes (founding acts, lineage, mandate instruments) are distinguished from transitory ones; deletion is reconciled with the reconstruction horizon and with tombstone resolvability; legal holds suspend disposition.

Versioned crosswalks to W3C ORG, CPOV, FHIR, LDAP, SCIM, schema.org and ISO/IEC 6523, each with direction and fidelity notes. Projection loss is declared and re-import is prohibited, because LDAP 'ou' and SCIM department/division carry only names.
Kind codes are scheme-bound and versioned, following org:classification and CPOV's code-valued purpose and classification; multi-scheme coding is supported with a governing-scheme flag.

Mandate scope, delegating instrument, quantitative authority limits, sub-delegation rules and assurance processes are modelled on ISO 37000 guidance. The full ISO 37000 text is paywalled; only the ISO/TC 309 committee overview was reviewed, so this is guidance-grade rather than requirement-grade support.

Headcount and FTE are treated as dated measurement events with declared basis, population definition, preparer and restatement handling, constrained by ESRS S1-6's headcount/FTE and breakdown requirements.

Individual occupancy is excluded by boundary; only unit-level aggregates are held; minimum cell size suppression and prohibited breakdown combinations are modelled. Specific data-protection legal bases are deferred to a privacy model.

Handled as a bounded reference: mandate spatial coverage is in scope via CPOV's spatial property, but premises, addresses and geometry are excluded because FHIR separates Location from Organization and Eurostat's local unit is a statistical geographic construct.

Communities of practice, informal influence networks, temporary task forces below the establishment threshold and de facto reporting that diverges from the recorded chart are not modelled. No authoritative source was found that normatively defines these, so they are recorded as a gap rather than invented.

Works councils, union structures and co-determination bodies interact with reorganization but are only referenced as a precondition on the act. Their own composition, election cycles and rights vary by jurisdiction and are left to a dedicated model; no primary source was retrieved during this research.

known_omissions: Full texts of ISO 37000:2021, ISO 30414:2018, ISO 15489-1:2016 and ISO/IEC 6523-1:2023 are paywalled. Only committee overview material, catalogue metadata, the Peppol ICD deployment and secondary summaries were reviewed, so ISO-derived structure is guidance-grade rather than verified against normative clause text.

Council Regulation (EEC) No 696/93 could not be retrieved directly from EUR-Lex during this research; the statistical-unit boundary rests on the Eurostat Statistics Explained glossary entry that cites it.

The ESRS S1 delegated act annex PDF was retrieved but not machine-parseable; the S1-6 headcount and breakdown requirements are stated at summary level and should be verified against clause text before any compliance claim.

Military, ecclesiastical, academic-collegiate and cooperative governance structures have unit forms (regiments, dioceses, faculties, chapters) that are not specifically accommodated beyond the generic kind code list.
Capacity and skills held by a unit, budget allocation mechanics, and process or capability ownership are deliberately excluded and would need sibling models.
No modelling of unit-level performance objectives, KPIs or scorecards; these were judged to belong to a performance-management model.
Cross-organization joint ventures and shared-service entities that sit between two parents are only partially handled through affiliations; their dual-ownership structure is unresolved.
conflicts: W3C ORG binds org:reportsTo to Agents and Posts, not to organizational units. Unit-to-unit reporting lines - which the previous O2 material asserted directly - are therefore an extension of the standard and are recorded as non-conformant use with an explicit mapping rule.

FHIR R5 has no distinct organizational-unit class: departments are Organization instances chained by partOf. This conflicts with W3C ORG's separate OrganizationalUnit class and with CPOV's reuse of it; exports to FHIR flatten the distinction and must declare the loss.

schema.org's parentOrganization (superseding branchOf) does not distinguish an internal department from an owned subsidiary, conflating containment with ownership. The crosswalk must add an edge-semantics qualifier that schema.org cannot carry.

RFC 4519 'ou' and RFC 7643 department/division are name-valued and multi-valued, with no identifier, validity period or typed edge. Round-tripping through a directory is lossy in a way that cannot be repaired, so directory content is never authoritative.

ROR and GLEIF both decline to identify internal subdivisions - ROR because departments 'often emerge, close, combine, and change', GLEIF because an LEI represents one legal entity. There is therefore no governed global identifier for most units, and ISO/IEC 6523's organization part identifier is the only standard slot, with ambiguity about who assigns it.
IFRS 8 permits aggregation of operating segments with similar economic characteristics, so a reportable segment is not a unit and a one-to-one mapping between units and segments cannot be assumed.
CPOV constrains purpose to COFOG codes suited to public administration; that scheme is inapplicable to private-sector units, so purpose coding is scheme-dependent rather than universal.

Eurostat's local unit is defined by geographic situation, whereas an internal unit is defined by mandate and reporting. Treating an office or site as an organizational unit conflates the two and produces incorrect statistical reporting.
regional_assumptions: CPOV, ESRS S1 and the statistical-unit framework are EU instruments; their applicability outside the EU is by voluntary adoption only.
NARA General Records Schedules bind US federal agencies only; they are used here as a model for governed disposition authority, not as a generally applicable rule.

Employee information and consultation duties before a reorganization takes effect vary sharply - strong in several continental European jurisdictions, weak or absent elsewhere - so consultation is modelled as an optional, jurisdiction-conditioned precondition on a reorganization act.

Public-sector units in some jurisdictions have statutory existence published in an official gazette, giving them an external authority that private units lack; the model accommodates this through the dual-classification flag but does not enumerate national regimes.
Minimum cell size thresholds for staffing disclosure are set by national data-protection practice and collective agreements, so the threshold is a Dimension parameter rather than a fixed value.
ISO/IEC 6523 ICD availability is uneven by country; the Peppol list reflects European e-invoicing deployment more densely than other regions.
Financial reporting alignment assumes IFRS; US GAAP ASC 280 uses a comparable management approach but differs in detail and was not researched.
adversarial_checks: Searched for a governed global identifier for internal units. ROR states it is 'not focused on capturing all subdivisions of a given organization such as a university's schools or departments' and GLEIF issues LEIs only to legal entities. The attractive assumption of a global unit IRI was rejected; unit identity is parent-scoped by default with ISO/IEC 6523 organization part identification as the only standard external slot.

Tested whether unit-to-unit reporting lines have standards support. W3C ORG defines org:reportsTo between Agents or Posts, not units, so the previous version's unit-level reportingLine object is an extension. Retained because matrix management is real, but demoted to a declared non-conformant extension rather than presented as canonical.

Tested whether sites, offices and branches belong in this model. FHIR states Location records where a service occurs while Organization records who performed it, and Eurostat's local unit is defined by geographic situation. Rejected folding premises into unit structure; branches that are separately registered are handled by dual classification instead.

Tested whether established positions belong here or in WM-ORG-004. W3C ORG's Post 'exists independently of who fills it', and the registry assigns Position its own model, so only the unit-side establishment count, seating and aggregate occupancy were retained. The previous version's full establishedPosition object was rejected as a boundary violation.

Tested whether a single containment tree is sufficient. IFRS 8's management approach makes the internal reporting hierarchy decisive for segment identification, which may differ from the legal or cost roll-up. Single-parent-only structure was rejected in favour of named concurrent hierarchies with per-hierarchy single-parent constraints.

Tested whether reorganization can be modelled as attribute edits on unit records. W3C ORG's ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultingOrganization requires many-to-many lineage that attribute edits cannot express, and ROR retains relationships on inactive records as tombstones. Attribute-edit modelling was rejected.

Tested whether directory and HR systems could serve as the source of truth. RFC 4519 and RFC 7643 carry unit information as bare names without identifiers, validity or typed edges, so any round-trip silently destroys governed structure. Re-import was prohibited outright rather than merely discouraged.

Tested whether headcount is a unit attribute. ESRS S1-6 requires declared basis, breakdowns and methodology disclosure, and figures differ by point-in-time versus average convention. Attribute modelling was rejected in favour of dated measurement events with an explicit basis and separate observation timestamp.
